cases.exposure_context_quote: A 22-year-old man with no significant past medical history, weighing 65 kg, was brought to the emergency department approximately three hours after intentional ingestion of a full 100 mL commercial container of 5% emamectin benzoate emulsifiable concentrate (EC) pesticide formulation.
cases.agent_quote: intentional ingestion of a full 100 mL commercial container of 5% emamectin benzoate emulsifiable concentrate (EC) pesticide formulation
cases.circumstance: intentional ingestion of full 100 mL commercial container

symptoms.finding: coma (GCS 6/15), bilaterally dilated reactive pupils, hypotonia, absent deep tendon reflexes
symptoms.quote: On arrival, he was unconscious, with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 6/15 (E1V1M4), bilaterally dilated but reactive pupils, generalized hypotonia, and absent deep tendon reflexes.

symptoms.finding: refractory shock despite fluids and norepinephrine
symptoms.quote: the patient continued to exhibit refractory, vasopressor-dependent shock, with blood pressure remaining approximately 80/50 mmHg
The patient underwent immediate endotracheal intubation and was placed on mechanical ventilation using synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation with volume control (SIMV-VC) mode

symptoms.finding: severe mixed respiratory-metabolic acidosis, hypokalemia, hypocalcemia, elevated lactate
symptoms.quote: Initial investigations revealed leukocytosis, hypoxemia, severe mixed respiratory-metabolic acidosis, hypokalemia, mild hypocalcemia, and an elevated serum lactate level of 4 mmol/L

labs.name: serum lactate
labs.quote: an elevated serum lactate level of 4 mmol/L, while renal and hepatic functions remained preserved (Table 1)

labs.name: CVP
labs.quote: revealing a low central venous pressure (CVP) of 3 cmH2O, suggestive of significant intravascular volume depletion

treatment.name: intubation and mechanical ventilation (SIMV-VC)
treatment.quote: The patient underwent immediate endotracheal intubation and was placed on mechanical ventilation using synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation with volume control (SIMV-VC) mode

treatment.name: gastric lavage and activated charcoal
treatment.quote: gastric lavage and activated charcoal were administered despite presentation beyond the conventional decontamination window

treatment.name: norepinephrine titrated to 0.8 mcg/kg/min
treatment.quote: The dose was escalated to a peak of 0.8 mcg/kg/min, yet the patient continued to exhibit refractory, vasopressor-dependent shock

treatment.name: rescue intravenous lipid emulsion (Celepid 10%, initial bolus 3 mL/kg = 195 mL, then 0.5 mL/kg/min for 30 min; second bolus at 14 h)
treatment.quote: rescue therapy with ILE was initiated nine hours after ingestion (five hours after ICU admission)

cases.outcome: hemodynamic recovery after first ILE dose, neurological improvement after second dose; survived
cases.outcome_quote: Hemodynamic recovery followed the first dose, and neurological improvement was observed after the second dose.
